title: Join, All Ye Servants of the Lord
description: Join, All Ye Servants of the Lord in Tonic Solfa to SELENA, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 187 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Praise to God for his Word”, where the book credits them to the Spirit of the Psalms.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SELENA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Join, all ye ser-vants of the Lord, To praise him for his sa-cred word, That word, like man-na, sent from heaven, To all who seek it free-ly given; Its prom-is-es our fears re-move, And fill our hearts with joy and love.

lines: Join, all ye servants of the Lord,
To praise him for his sacred word, —
That word, like manna, sent from heaven,
To all who seek it freely given;
And fill our hearts with joy and love.
It tells us, though oppressed with cares,
The God of mercy hears our prayers;
Though steep and rough th' appointed way,
His mighty arm shall be our stay;
Though deadly foes assail our peace,
His power shall bid their malice cease.
It tells who first inspired our breath,
And who redeemed our souls from death;
It tells of grace, — grace freely given, —
And shows the path to God and heaven:
O, bless we, then, our gracious Lord,
For all the treasures of his word.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SELENA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
